item.title: Andalusia Council honors Baumgartner
item.description: Andalusia Council honors state DYW winner Mia Baumgartner, sets July 17–19 back-to-school tax holiday, and names delegates for upcoming municipal league meeting.

item.title: Senn joins Mizell as new provider
item.description: Vicki Senn, CRNP, joins Mizell Clinic 2 in Opp, offering comprehensive primary care, DOT physicals and chronic disease management starting March 2, 2026.

item.title: Hughes receives 18 Under 31 Young Alumni Award
item.description: UA electrical engineering alumnus Landon Hughes, a PowerSouth Energy distribution engineer supporting 500,000 cooperative members, earns a 2026 18 Under 31 Young Alumni Award.

item.title: 20th Cancer Freeze is an unmitigated success
item.description: 20th Cancer Freeze in Florala raises over $100,000 for five local cancer patients, capping two decades of community events that have donated $2 million to families within 100 miles.

item.title: DAR’S GOOD CITIZENS
item.description: Old Three Notch DAR honors Covington County students with 2025-26 Good Citizen and Youth Leadership awards at Andalusia City Hall ceremony.

item.description: Explore the full digital version of our February 25, 2026 issue and stay updated with the latest news and features.

item.description: Explore the 2026 Andalusia Area Chamber of Commerce Directory, including this year's Award winners, events schedule, membership directory, and more.

item.title: LBW’s Saints take the Stage on March 6 and 7
item.description: LBW Community College hosts its fifth annual “Saints on Stage” variety show March 6–7, 7–9 p.m., at the Dixon Center in Andalusia, showcasing student and community talent to raise project funds.

item.title: Damascus Baptist to welcome The Golden Aires
item.description: The Golden Aires Gospel Quartet will perform at Damascus Baptist Church on March 13 from 6–7 p.m., with refreshments after the service and all attendees welcome.

item.title: CAN GOD UNDERSTAND HOW WE FEEL?
item.description: A vivid courtroom-style parable wrestles with whether God really knows human suffering, ending with the claim that God has already shared our deepest pain.
